events.text: ❗️Ukrainian drones targeted the Voronezhsintezkauchuk plant in Voronezh overnight, with locals reporting explosions and Russian air-defense activity. The SIBUR-owned chemical facility is a major producer of synthetic rubber, latex and thermoplastic elastomers. Its products are used across automotive, heavy machinery, aviation and other industrial sectors, including rubber goods, tires, gaskets and seals.

events.text: ❗️Ukrainian long-range drones struck the Perm oil refinery in Russia this morning, with multiple fires reported across the facility. Located around 1,500 km from Ukraine, the LUKOIL-operated plant is one of Russia’s largest refineries, with annual crude processing capacity of about 13.1 million tons. It produces more than 60 petroleum products, including gasoline, diesel, aviation fuel, bitumen and lubricants.

events.title: Telegram
events.text:
Two IDF reservists were killed yesterday after a small explosive drone they were operating in the Gaza Strip crashed for an unknown reason and exploded shortly after, the military announces.
The troops are named as Master Sgt. (res.) Nadav Kali, 24, from Har Halutz, and Master Sgt. (res.) Ofek Moalem, 23, from Jerusalem. 
Both served in the Jerusalem Brigade's 7007th Battalion.
According to a preliminary investigation by the military, the two soldiers on Thursday afternoon had been operating first-person view (FPV) drones known as "Atalef" -- Hebrew for bat -- from an army post inside the military's Gaza buffer zone in the Strip's north.
A first drone carried out its intended mission, while a second, during its takeoff, crashed inside the army post for an as-yet-unknown reason. The soldiers approached the crashed drone several minutes later, picked it up, and it then exploded, fatally wounding them, according to the initial probe.
The pair were taken to Barzilai Hospital in Ashkelon, where their deaths were declared.
Amid the investigation into the cause of the crash and explosion, the military has temporarily grounded all small drones capable of carrying explosive payloads -- both suicide drones and those that drop their explosives on a target.

🔥I’m not lovin’ it: Russia strikes warehouse used by McDonald’s near Kiev
 
A drone strike targeting a warehouse ~20km from central Kiev has threatened McDonald’s Ukrainian operations with widespread supply disruptions.
Packed with fresh and frozen goods including patties, nuggets, fries, buns, deserts and sauces, the strike adds to McDonald’s local headaches – with its operations already impacted by menu cuts and logistical problems.
It’s not clear what sorts of military or dual-use items alongside patties and buns it may have contained, if any.

🇨🇳 China’s unique next-gen jet spotted soaring over Chengdu as Xi visits Washington
 
The unmistakable, tailless delta-diamond design of the new J-36 sixth-gen aircraft was spotted performing a test flight in southwestern China.
The flight coincided with[ Xi’s trip to the US](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/75088), where he was treated to a military flyover.
Besides its shape, the J-36 is packed with unique features, including trijet engine configuration for super cruise (and improved survivability), and unusual dorsal and ventral air intakes.
👉 Classified as a ‘stealth fighter’, the J-36 is really more of an airborne cruiser. With a 19-20M wingspan, 22-23M length and 50-55T estimated takeoff weight, the jet’s internal weapons payload could be 6T+.
Potential strike power includes ultra-long-range AAMs to take on enemy AWACS or tankers, anti-ship missiles, standoff precision-guided munitions, and possibly lasers.
The jet could serve as a flying command node, and has a twin, side-by-side seating configuration – exceptionally rare in modern tactical aircraft.
The US has [nothing like it.](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/69329)

events.text:
🔨Initiative for US-Iran talks finds resistance among Persian Gulf oil producers
The UAE and Saudi Arabia are lobbying the Trump administration to keep up the pressure on Iran and not agree to concessions that would ease sanctions or the US Navy blockade, The Wall Street Journal reports.
➡️ Recently, regional mediators, including Qatar, have been pressing for renewed dialogue between the warring states, with a new round possibly happening in Oman as soon as next week, while President Donald Trump claims that a meeting with Iran is coming soon.
Despite the current rhetoric, Arab states led by Saudi Arabia had pushed for negotiations with Iran throughout the summer months and were even willing to acknowledge some Iranian sway over the Strait of Hormuz — but rolled back the initiative as the conflict with Yemen’s Houthis escalated.
Currently, Iran aims to return to conditions identified in June’s Memorandum of Understanding, which promised sanctions relief, access to Iranian frozen assets, and an administrative role in the Strait of Hormuz.
